title: Meta and chip stocks decline as AI trade comes under pressure
content:
Good morning. Stocks declined on Thursday as semiconductor names fell, with the AI trade unwinding following quarterly results from Meta (META) and Tesla (TSLA).
Shares of the EV maker recovered early trading losses while Meta sank 6%.
The Tech (XLK) sector fell, led by chipmakers like Nvidia (NVDA) and AMD (AMD). Memory makers Micron (MU) and SK Hynix (SKHY) also dropped as the chip sector reversed gains from Wednesday.
Shares of the wafer equipment maker Lam Research (LRCX) fell as much as 10% after management pointed to "supply chain constraints" heading into 2027.
Here's a check of the markets in the first few minutes of trading, based on a heat map powered by Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data.
Brent crude oil futures (BZ=F) jumped to a five-month high at $112 per barrel while WTI (CL=F) traded near $100 after a report of possible US and Israeli attacks on Iran after the November midterm elections.
Here are some other notable stocks that Yahoo Finance readers are viewing this morning: IBM (IBM), Lockheed Martin (LMT), and Procter & Gamble (PG).

report.summary: Meta and chip stocks fell as the AI trade unwound after quarterly results, with Lam Research warning of supply constraints and oil rising on geopolitical risk.
report.background: The AI trade has been one of the strongest equity-market themes, concentrated in mega-cap platforms and semiconductor suppliers seen as beneficiaries of data-center buildouts. That concentration makes the group vulnerable to any sign that earnings, capital spending, or supply chains may disappoint. Thursday’s session showed that sensitivity: quarterly results from Meta and Tesla triggered a rotation, while chipmakers reversed prior gains. Lam Research’s warning about supply-chain constraints into 2027 added a specific hardware bottleneck concern. At the same time, oil jumped on reports of possible US–Israeli attacks on Iran after the November midterms, adding macro and geopolitical risk. The article is a market snapshot, not a full earnings analysis, but it captures how quickly the AI narrative can shift from momentum to valuation and execution scrutiny.
key_points: Meta shares fell 6% after its quarterly results, making it a visible drag on mega-cap tech sentiment. The article does not detail the results, but the move shows investors are quick to punish perceived AI-related disappointment or spending concerns. Tesla recovered early losses, highlighting divergent reactions to earnings.

Chip stocks led the tech sector lower, with Nvidia and AMD declining and memory makers Micron and SK Hynix also dropping. The selloff reversed gains from Wednesday, suggesting fragile momentum in semiconductor names tied to AI demand. Because chips underpin data-center AI, their moves are a proxy for investor confidence in the buildout.

Lam Research fell as much as 10% after management flagged 'supply chain constraints' heading into 2027. That is notable because chip-equipment makers sit upstream of AI hardware; constraints can delay capacity expansion and raise costs. The warning turned a broad AI-trade worry into a concrete supply-chain risk for the semiconductor cycle.

Oil prices jumped, with Brent at a five-month high of $112 and WTI near $100, after a report of possible US and Israeli attacks on Iran after the November midterms. Higher energy prices can feed inflation and complicate the macro backdrop for risk assets, adding pressure alongside the AI-trade unwind.

The market reaction was not uniform: Tesla recovered early losses while Meta and chip names stayed weak. IBM, Lockheed Martin, and Procter & Gamble were also among notable stocks readers watched. The mix suggests investors are rotating rather than exiting risk entirely.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the session reinforces that the trade is now more sensitive to earnings execution, capital-spending discipline, and hardware supply chains than to narrative alone. A Lam Research supply warning into 2027 could signal longer lead times or higher costs for chip capacity, which matters for data-center expansion. Developers may see indirect effects through cloud GPU pricing, availability, and vendor roadmaps if capex is scrutinized. Regular users are less immediately exposed, but slower AI feature rollouts or higher subscription/API prices could follow if companies tighten spending. The oil spike adds broad macro risk that can hit tech valuations regardless of AI fundamentals.
report.tools: To follow this theme, watch Yahoo Finance and its AlphaSpace heat maps for sector moves; OpenBB and yfinance for open-source market data; TradingView and Finviz for chip-stock screening; SEC EDGAR for earnings filings and capex commentary; and FRED for oil and macro indicators. For supply-chain signals, track Lam Research, Nvidia, AMD, Micron, and SK Hynix earnings calls and guidance. These tools help separate broad AI-trade sentiment from company-specific execution and hardware bottlenecks.
